title: Hadwiger's Conjecture
statement_text: Every graph with chromatic number at least $t$ contains the complete graph $K_t$ on $t$ vertices as a minor.
context_text: Hadwiger conjectured this in 1943; it remains wide open for every $t \geq 7$. The paper focuses on the special case $\alpha(G) \leq 2$, where the conjecture predicts a $K_{\lceil|V(G)|/2\rceil}$ minor, described as "still very challenging" even in this restricted setting.
paper_contribution: Proves that every graph $G$ with $\alpha(G) \leq 2$ contains a minor $H$ with $|V(H)| = \lceil|V(G)|/2\rceil$ and at least $(\gamma - o(1))\binom{|V(H)|}{2}$ edges where $\gamma = 0.986882\ldots$, establishing a dense minor of the exact size predicted by the conjecture for this case (fewer than $1/76$ of all possible edges missing), as progress toward the complete minor.
paper_title: Dense minors of graphs with independence number two

title: Informal conjecture on improving the $g(t)$ lower bound
statement_text: The factor $1/4$ in $g(t) \geq t(t+2)/8$ can likely be significantly improved. However it appears to be quite challenging, for example, to show that every graph with chromatic number at least $t$ contains a minor on $t$ vertices with at most one tenth of all possible edges missing.
context_text: Graphs are simple. $g(t)$ is the largest integer such that every graph with chromatic number at least $t$ contains a minor with exactly $t$ vertices and at least $g(t)$ edges; Hadwiger's conjecture asserts $g(t)=\binom{t}{2}$. Since every graph with chromatic number at least $t$ has a subgraph of minimum degree at least $t-1$, and Mader showed that every graph of average degree at least $t-1$ has a minor on at most $t$ vertices with minimum degree at least $t/2$, one gets $g(t)\ge t(t+2)/8=\frac14\binom{t}{2}+o(t^2)$. The authors believe the factor $1/4$ can be significantly improved but find even density $9/10$ challenging. They concentrate instead on graphs $G$ with independence number $\alpha(G)\le2$ (where Hadwiger's conjecture would give a $K_{\lceil|V(G)|/2\rceil}$ minor and Duchet–Meyniel gives $K_{\lceil|V(G)|/3\rceil}$), and prove that such $G$ has a minor on $\lceil|V(G)|/2\rceil$ vertices missing fewer than $1/76$ of all possible edges (edge density at least $0.98688\ldots-o(1)$).
notes: Stated as a remark in the introduction without a labelled environment; language 'can likely' and 'appears to be quite challenging' signals authorial belief rather than a formal conjecture.
paper_title: Dense minors of graphs with independence number two
